newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW plans to introduce new mini-car - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: VW plans to introduce new mini-car - newspaper.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG will soon introduce a new mini-car to will be built at its main factory in a bid to prove that small vehicles can be profitably built in Germany, according to a German newspaper.
The Frankfurt Allgemeine Zeitung reported in its Saturday edition that VW will soon unveil the VW Lupino, which is slated to be offered to the public during 1997.
VW, Europe's largest carmaker, will also offer a similar vehicle from its Spanish subsidiary SEAT which will be called the "Arosa". It will be introduced before the VW version.

The SEAT version of the four-seat vehicle, which is based on a shortened platform of the subcompact VW Polo but uses the same engine, will cost about 17,000 marks ($11,000). The better-equipped Lupino will be more expensive, the newspaper said.

VW officials have previously said the new car will compete in the so-called "sub-B" competitive market segement against the Ford Ka, Renault Twingo, the Fiat Cinquecentro and other minicars, such as the planned Mercedes Swatch vehicle set for introduction next year.
The vehicle will also be the model for VW to consider producing a so-called "three-liter" auto aimed at reducing energy consumption.

A spokesman for Wolfsburg-based VW was not available at the weekend for comment on the new vehicle, which is the developed version of the concept car Chico that was first shown at the 1991 Frankfurt auto show.

The newspaper said VW wanted to build the vehicle at its Wolfsburg plant to demonstrate that small vehicles can be made in Germany at a profit despite the country's higher wage costs and also to take advantage of excess production capacity.

The new vehicle, called the EA 420 at VW, can be built in about seven hours, which is about half the prodution time of the subcompact VW polo and about a quarter of the time needed to build the popular VW Golf, the newspaper said.
The vehicle relies heavily on new work practices as well as heavy outsourcing of parts and materials to reduce costs and production time, according to the newspaper report.
VW has estimated that sales from vehicles built on the Polo and Lupino platforms will total about one million vehicles from the year 2000.
